Chasm Explorer, Sussex East
r.description: Explore ancient chalk downland & the deepest dry valley in the country. Discover where the Devil & his wife are buried, watch kestrels in the Sussex countryside & visit an ancient farmstead with over 1,000 years of history. Some steep ascents & descents.

r.name: Ditchling Beacon to Devil's Dyke, South Downs walk, Sussex East
r.description: This walk takes in one of the most stunning sections of the South Downs Way. Spring & Summer bring rich plant life thanks to the chalk soil, forming unique grassland habitat. Great bus links from Brighton. Mostly flat until Pyecombe where it gets steep.

r.name: Wolstonbury Hill Explore Nature Walk, Sussex East
r.description: Go through beech woodland before climbing steep open grassland to the top of the hill. On summiting, admire panoramic views of the weald, sea & downs, including Newtimber Hill & Devil's Dyke. Bluebells & garlic can be found in Spring. Potential livestock.

r.name: Saddlescombe Farm and Newtimber walk, Sussex East
r.description: A scenic ancient landscape can be expected on this downland walk near Devils Dyke. Discover the wildlife-rich dewpond & glimpse into the past at the Donkey Wheel. Short, steep ascent to start then gently undulating, grassy terrain. Dogs welcome on leads

r.name: Fulking Archaeology Walk, Sussex East
r.description: A circular route from The Devil's Dyke pub. An archaeological walk through time, along the glorious contours of the Sussex Downs. On one side is the Weald, with the sea on the other. Downland & field paths, with some stiles. Keep dogs under close control.

r.name: Rampart Ramble, Sussex East
r.description: Stroll around the old walls of the Iron Age hill fort. Take in views over the Weald & Brighton. Look out for remains of the curious Victorian funfair riders & in summer, walk through a meadow of orchids & butterflies. Suitable for pushchairs when dry

r.name: Download Discovery walk, Sussex East
r.description: A slightly challenging walk taking in the north face of the hill fort & looping back through the wood to the north of the valley & meadow. Stunning views & a walk over ancient downland. Discover peace & quiet on one of the busiest hills on the South Downs

r.name: A Walk at Blackcap, Blackcap
r.description: Enjoy a circular walk around this secluded gem with sunken bostals, a hidden woodland, views over the Weald and fascinating history. 'Bostal' is a Sussex term for a way up a hill on the South Downs. Uneven ground, muddy in wet weather. 1 stile.
